work_done: Reviewed Phase 2 (channel-neutral core + reversible gcs_* to object_key rename) against PHASE_2_SPEC.md and the executor diff, and authored PHASE_3_SPEC.md. Verified AC4: app/inbound.py defines InboundMessage + handle_inbound importing no WhatsApp types (AST test passes), app/channels/whatsapp.py is a thin to_inbound/from_reply adapter, app/retrieval.answer_query is WhatsApp-type-free, app/main.py webhook routes the non-serve_v1 branch through the adapter into handle_inbound with request.app.state.store, and handle_inbound is a faithful line-by-line port of pipeline.handle_message; the Phase 1 caller mismatch was fixed (admin/batches.py uses get_object_store; intake.handle_image_inbound is channel-neutral). Verified AC5: migration 007 is idempotent with a documented exact inverse and is registered in apply_migrations.py FILES; app/db.py carries synonym() for gcs_object on papers/pending_papers/image_batch_items and served_object on papers; app/config.py carries AliasChoices for GCS_BUCKET/MEDIA_GCS_PREFIX/CONTRIBUTION_GCS_PREFIX. Found three defects (flagged, not overruled): (1) a live-serve-path regression introduced in Phase 2 Part B where raw-SQL SELECT labels were renamed to object_key/served_object_key but the .mappings() consumers still read the old keys, raising KeyError at app/retrieval.py:253-254/265/268 (load_served_bytes_v1), app/retrieval.py:321-322 (load_served_cached, swallowed into a silent permanent cache miss then falling through to the broken path), and app/serve_index.py:94 (_row_to_candidate); (2) raw-SQL literals still naming the old column on the renamed pending_papers table at review/promote.py:44, review/main.py:375, and cloud_ingest/main.py:114-115 (the contribution_pages literals are correct as-is since that table is not renamed); (3) the spec-required tests/test_object_key_rename.py was never written, leaving AC5 synonym/env-alias/migration-shape with no automated guard. These three are carried into PHASE_3_SPEC.md as mandatory opportunistic cleanups. The full suite was not run here because the sandbox runs Python 3.14 while the project targets 3.12 and conftest's db_session fixture does not resolve; the carried KeyError fixes are what a full 3.12 run would surface. PHASE_3_SPEC.md specifies the in-house plumbing phase (AC6, AC7): filesystem/MinIO ObjectStore behind the existing port, backend-issued HMAC-signed ~15-minute download URLs with a verifying /download route, a file/env SecretsProvider, a plain-Postgres EngineProvider, bearer-token auth for the future tool endpoint, and removal of the plaintext DB password/Cloud SQL string from apply_migrations.py and the hardcoded GCP project id from infra_bootstrap.sh/scripts/restore_drill.sh/Dockerfile, following the established spec structure. Committed PHASE_3_SPEC.md.
next_steps: Phase 3 Part A: app/signing.py HMAC sign/verify, add ObjectStore.signed_url to the port, implement FsObjectStore (and optional MinioObjectStore), add GET /download verifying signature+expiry and POST /tool/retrieve, wire the local/minio provider branches, with signing and filesystem tests.

Fix the Phase 2 carried-over defects while touching those paths: re-point the .mappings() reads in app/retrieval.py and app/serve_index.py to the new column labels; re-point the pending_papers raw-SQL literals in review/promote.py, review/main.py, and cloud_ingest/main.py to object_key; and add the missing tests/test_object_key_rename.py.
Confirm AC1 (full pytest suite green) in the project's real Python 3.12 environment where conftest's db_session fixture resolves.
open_questions: AC1 full-suite greenness is unverified in this sandbox (Python 3.14 vs the project's 3.12; conftest db_session fixture does not resolve), so only the Phase 2 focused tests were observed as passing; the carried-over serve-path KeyError fixes are expected to be what a full 3.12 run surfaces.

cloud_ingest/ is frozen tooling not run against prod, but it shares the same database and its INSERT INTO pending_papers (... gcs_object ...) will break post-migration; the Phase 3 cleanup re-points it, but whether cloud_ingest is ever re-run in the self-hosted deployment is a product decision outside this review.
